newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's China Motor plans T$2/shr div.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's China Motor plans T$2/shr div.

text.p: China Motor Co, one of Taiwan's top two car makers, said on Thursday it plans to issue dividends of T$2 per share for 1996.
The dividends include a cash dividend of T$1.5 per share and a stock dividend, or bonus issue, of T$0.5 per share, the company said in a statement.
China Motor has set a 1997 pre-tax profit target of T$2.4 billion on sales of T$40 billion, compared with a 1996 pre-tax profit of T$2.197 billion on sales of T$31.06 billion, it said.
For 1997, it plans to sell 97,000 cars, up from 77,249 in 1996, the statement said.

The firm said it would introduce two new models in the second half -- a 2,400 cc Space Gear multipurpose vehicle and a 2,000 cc Worldwide Car, which like its other models are made under licence from Japan's Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
The second is made of parts from Asian suppliers.
China Motor said it had decided to set up a venture capital firm with Yulon Motor Co, which makes cars under licence with Japan's Nissan Motor Co Ltd.

The T$1 billion firm, with China Motor investing T$495 million to take a 49.5 percent stake, will focus on investment in high-technology businesses such as information, telecommunications, consumer electronics, semiconductors and key electronics parts and components, it said.
